title: Liver blood tests
subtitle: Bilirubin, ALT, ALP, GGT, albumin and synthetic function
summary: Bilirubin, ALT, ALP, GGT, albumin and synthetic function
introduction: “LFTs” contain markers of hepatocyte injury, cholestasis and synthetic function. ALT, ALP and bilirubin describe patterns of injury; albumin and INR help assess synthetic function but are influenced by other conditions.

rows.name: ALT
rows.referenceRange: RVH adult reference: male <41 U/L; female <33 U/L
highInterpretation: Hepatocellular injury. Causes include fatty liver disease, viral hepatitis, alcohol-related injury, medicines, ischaemia and autoimmune hepatitis.

rows.name: ALP
lowInterpretation: Can occur with malnutrition, zinc deficiency, hypothyroidism or rare metabolic disorders.
highInterpretation: Cholestasis or biliary obstruction, but also bone disease, healing fracture, pregnancy and growth. Use GGT to support hepatic origin.

rows.name: GGT
rows.referenceRange: RVH adult reference: male 10–71 U/L; female 6–42 U/L
highInterpretation: Supports hepatic origin of raised ALP. Can rise with alcohol, cholestasis, fatty liver and enzyme-inducing medicines; it is non-specific.

rows.name: Bilirubin
highInterpretation: Pre-hepatic haemolysis, hepatocellular dysfunction or biliary obstruction. Visible jaundice often appears around 40–60 micromol/L but varies.

rows.name: Albumin
lowInterpretation: Chronic liver dysfunction, inflammation, malnutrition, renal or gastrointestinal protein loss, or dilution. It changes slowly and is not a sensitive marker of acute liver injury.
highInterpretation: Usually haemoconcentration from reduced plasma volume.

rows.name: INR / prothrombin time
rows.referenceRange: Use local range; interpret separately when taking warfarin
highInterpretation: Can indicate reduced hepatic synthesis, vitamin K deficiency, anticoagulant effect or DIC. In acute liver injury, a rising INR is an important marker of failure.

rows.name: Hepatocellular pattern
highInterpretation: Consider viral, metabolic, autoimmune, drug-induced or ischaemic hepatocyte injury.

rows.name: Cholestatic pattern
rows.referenceRange: ALP rise predominates, often with GGT and bilirubin
highInterpretation: Consider gallstone obstruction, biliary infection, pancreatic/biliary malignancy, drug-induced cholestasis or infiltrative disease.

rows.name: Mixed pattern
rows.referenceRange: Both ALT and ALP substantially raised
highInterpretation: Consider drug injury, infection, obstruction with hepatocyte injury or another mixed hepatic process.

rows.name: Isolated bilirubin rise
rows.referenceRange: Other enzymes normal or minimally changed
highInterpretation: Consider Gilbert syndrome, haemolysis or an early/partial obstructive process; assess conjugated fraction where available.

urgentFindings: Jaundice with fever, right-upper-quadrant pain, hypotension or new confusion: consider ascending cholangitis and urgent hospital assessment.
Acute liver injury with confusion, drowsiness, hypoglycaemia, bleeding, rising INR or metabolic acidosis: consider acute liver failure.
Very large new ALT rise, particularly into the thousands, with hypotension, overdose risk, medication change or viral symptoms.
Raised bilirubin with pale stool, dark urine, pruritus, weight loss or a palpable gallbladder requires prompt obstructive/malignancy assessment.
Albumin alone should not be used to diagnose acute liver failure; check INR, glucose, mental state and the overall clinical picture.
overrides: Use the reporting laboratory’s reference ranges and compare with previous results, symptoms, observations, medication and fluid status.

commonPatterns.title: Acute hepatocellular injury picture
findings: ALT markedly raised, predominating over ALP
Acute onset of symptoms (malaise, nausea, right-upper-quadrant discomfort) or a new medication/toxin exposure
interpretation: Suggests acute hepatocyte injury; consider viral hepatitis, drug-induced liver injury (including paracetamol overdose), ischaemic hepatitis, autoimmune hepatitis or alcohol-related injury
The degree of ALT rise and the trajectory (with INR and bilirubin) matter more than a single value for judging severity
actions: Take a focused history: medicines (including over-the-counter and herbal), alcohol, overdose risk, recent hypotensive episode and viral/travel exposure
Check INR and bilirubin alongside ALT to assess synthetic function and severity (see further testing)
Treat as time-critical if there is confusion, bleeding, rising INR or a very large ALT rise (see urgent findings)

commonPatterns.title: Cholestatic / obstructive picture
findings: ALP raised, supported by a raised GGT
Right-upper-quadrant pain, pale stool, dark urine or pruritus
interpretation: Suggests biliary obstruction or cholestasis; consider gallstones, biliary stricture, pancreatic/biliary malignancy or drug-induced cholestasis
Fever, right-upper-quadrant pain and jaundice together raise concern for ascending cholangitis, which is time-critical
actions: Assess for fever, rigors, hypotension or confusion suggesting cholangitis and treat as time-critical if present (see urgent findings)
Request FBC and CRP to support assessment of infection/inflammation, and consider imaging referral (see further testing)
Arrange prompt medical assessment for obstructive causes, particularly with pale stool, dark urine, pruritus, weight loss or a palpable gallbladder

commonPatterns.title: Mixed hepatocellular/cholestatic pattern
findings: Both ALT and ALP substantially raised
interpretation: Consider drug-induced liver injury, infection, obstruction with secondary hepatocyte injury, or another mixed hepatic process — the mixed pattern is less specific than a pure hepatocellular or cholestatic picture
actions: Review medication history in detail, including recently started or changed drugs
Request further testing to help localise the process (see further testing)
Arrange medical review for further work-up, especially if the derangement is marked or the patient is symptomatic

commonPatterns.title: Possible acute liver failure
findings: Markedly abnormal liver blood tests, often with a large ALT rise
interpretation: This combination suggests acute liver failure, a time-critical presentation — a rising INR reflects failing synthetic function and is a key severity marker, more so than the ALT level alone
Albumin changes slowly and should not be relied on to assess acute severity
actions: Treat as time-critical and arrange urgent hospital assessment (see urgent findings)
Check glucose immediately — hypoglycaemia is a recognised and dangerous feature of acute liver failure
Establish overdose risk (particularly paracetamol) and timing, as this changes the urgency and specific treatment available

commonPatterns.title: Isolated bilirubin rise
findings: ALT, ALP and GGT normal or minimally changed
interpretation: Consider Gilbert syndrome (common and benign, often intermittent and stress/fasting related), haemolysis, or an early/partial obstructive process too soon to raise other enzymes
Distinguishing these usually needs the conjugated/unconjugated split, which is not always available acutely
actions: Ask about a known history of Gilbert syndrome, fasting, intercurrent illness and pattern of previous mild jaundice
Request FBC and consider haemolysis screen if there are features of anaemia, dark urine or fatigue (see further testing)
Arrange routine follow-up if the patient is well; escalate if pale stool, dark urine or other obstructive features develop

rationale: INR is a key marker of hepatic synthetic function and severity in acute liver injury, and is followed serially to assess for evolving liver failure
Helps identify haemolysis as a cause of isolated bilirubin rise, and infection/inflammation contributing to a cholestatic picture
Supports assessment of an infective or inflammatory driver when a cholestatic or mixed pattern is present, particularly if cholangitis is suspected
Hypoglycaemia is a recognised and dangerous feature of acute liver failure and should be checked promptly when this is suspected
Essential when acute liver injury could be drug-induced or overdose is a possibility, as this determines specific antidote treatment and urgency
Needed to confirm or exclude biliary obstruction (gallstones, stricture, malignancy) in a cholestatic or mixed pattern

specimens.notes: Plasma — green-top lithium-heparin tube with yellow insert, 3 mL.
